MEASURED 2026-08-20 on the folded #262 tree, comparing reflow2's design-graph coupling against reflow2's ACTUAL Rust import graph (comments and string literals stripped first, because 2026-08-19 measured that 15% of a naive model is prose).

=== WHAT AGREES, AND IT IS MOST OF IT ===

The two models have THE SAME SHAPE and name THE SAME KERNEL. Blast radius = how many things transitively depend on you.

  design Components (56): median 0, mean 2.9, bimodal - 35 at zero, then nodes 30, provenance 29, schema 29, graph 28
  reflow2-core modules (53): median 1, mean 6.2, bimodal - 26 at zero, then nodes 46, provenance 44, identity 44, schema 43, graph 42

Four of the five kernel names are identical. The hand-authored DEPENDS_ON set is a FAITHFUL coupling model, sparser than the truth but not a different story. This is the same verdict the adopt run reached from the other direction: the sparse hand-authored edges were right.

=== WHAT DOES NOT AGREE, AND IT IS THE DANGEROUS HALF ===

18 Components carry NO PROVIDES, CONSUMES or DEPENDS_ON edge of any kind. Ten of those 18 map to a real source module by name. ALL TEN OF THOSE MODULES ARE COUPLED IN THE CODE - ten of ten, no exceptions:

  cmp:dto            design degree 0, code degree 11
  cmp:identity       design degree 0, code degree 5, and 44 of 52 modules transitively depend on it - a KERNEL module the design models as an island
  cmp:claims         0 / 4      cmp:alternatives  0 / 4
  sys:vocabulary     0 / 3      cmp:merge         0 / 3
  cmp:nudge          0 / 2      cmp:readiness     0 / 2
  cmp:degraded       0 / 1      cmp:sync          0 / 1

The remaining eight are the subsystems and cmp:docs / cmp:main / cmp:packaging, which have no single module to compare against.

=== WHY IT MATTERS FOR AN ARBITRARY USER'S PROJECT, NOT JUST THIS ONE ===

Ask reflow2 what breaks if you change cmp:identity and it answers NOTHING. The source says 44 of 52 modules. A false ZERO is the worst answer a coupling model can give: it is the most reassuring reply available and therefore the one least likely to be questioned - the exact doctrine reflow2 already applies to loop_status(contributor_id), where an unknown id is REFUSED rather than answered 'nothing is owed to you'.

And NOTHING IN REFLOW2 NOTICES. Every detector checks the CONSISTENCY OF EDGES THAT EXIST. A missing coupling edge is a defect of ABSENCE, and absence is the one thing the detector set does not ask about. The design is not wrong where it speaks; it is silent where it should speak, and silence reads as safety.

=== HOW IT WAS COMPUTED, SO IT CAN BE RE-RUN ===

Module graph: every crate::, super::, self:: and crate-name path in crates/*/src/**.rs after stripping comments and both string-literal forms, resolved to the longest known module prefix; grouped `use crate::{...}` forms confirmed absent (0 occurrences). Design graph: Component-to-Component DEPENDS_ON, plus CONSUMES-to-PROVIDES resolved through the Interface. Reverse-reachability closure on both. Cycle check re-run on the same model: reflow2-core 53 modules / 137 edges and reflow2-mcp 25 / 34, ZERO cycles at both top-module and file granularity - #262's claim independently confirmed.

STATED LIMIT, because the same trap is one day old: an import graph is COUPLING, not a contract. These numbers are the right input for 'where could a wall go' and the WRONG input for CONSUMES - importing them as contracts is exactly the mistake fact:adopt-ran-on-reflow2-and-the-mechanical-contract-recovery-collapsed records.
